messages:
sam.k: FYI — customer reported a voucher that worked yesterday now returns 422 via API. Dashboard still shows the code active. Customer says they changed the billing email on their account right before trying to redeem. Code: SPRINGFREE2026. Customer org: org_8241. Customer id: acct_9922. Paste of their curl below.

sam.k: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/claims 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***' 
 -d '{"code":"SPRINGFREE2026","account_id":"acct_9922"}' 
```

sam.k: Response: ```{
  "status":422,
  "error":"coupon_invalid",
  "message":"This voucher is invalid for the specified account."
}```

sam.k: They included request-id header: req_01H3Z7X9Z2Q8A1. Occurred at ~2026-03-16T15:12:05Z. Customer wants a manual credit if we can't repro quickly.

tanya: Thanks — can you drop the full request/response headers (sanitized) and the account -> org mapping? Also did they change primary email or did they move orgs/accounts? @eng-support can you take a look? :eyes:

sam.k: Pasted sanitized headers: ```Authorization: <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: req_01H3Z7X9Z2Q8A1
```

sam.k: The customer says they updated their billing email from marco@oldcorp.com -> marco@newcorp.com, but stayed in same org. No org transfer was requested.

eng-support: I'm seeing a 422 raised from the voucher service with code path set to validate account_org_id against voucher.allowed_orgs. Quick check: voucher SPRINGFREE2026 has allowed_orgs empty (global) but we have a tenant binding layer that maps accounts to tenant aliases for billing. After the email change a cache refresh job triggered and the tenant alias for acct_9922 temporarily returned null, so validation considered it a mismatch.

eng-support: Looking at logs for req_01H3Z7X9Z2Q8A1 -> voucher-service returned 422 because tenant_id was null. We have a race where profile updates invalidate the account->tenant cache and voucher validation path doesn't fall back to authoritative DB for a short window.

infra-oncall: Thanks for the signal. I see a recent Redis failover in the EU cluster at 15:11:58Z (node switchover completed in 6s). Some cache misses in the 15:12 window are expected. The application should have used DB fallback but there's a bug in the memoization layer.

eng-support: Repro steps: 1) update account email via /v1/accounts/:id PATCH 2) immediately POST /v1/claims with same account_id and code -> returns 422. If you wait 30s it succeeds.

eng-support: Quick mitigation options: (A) rebind tenant mapping in cache (manual flush) for acct_9922, (B) issue manual credit, (C) short-term hotfix to make voucher validation read-through DB on cache miss.

sam.k: Can we do (A) now and (B) while we wait? Customer is on a call.

infra-oncall: I flushed the account->tenant cache for acct_9922 (cache key tenant:acct_9922) at 15:20:10Z. Please retry.

sam.k: Retried internally with the same curl snippet, now response is 200 and claim succeeded. Customer confirmed they got the credit. :tada:

tanya: Punting to eng to schedule the memoization fallback fix. eng-support — can you create a ticket with repro and attach the Redis failover correlation? Also include suggested patch to check DB on cache miss.

eng-support: Will open ENG-1209 with logs, repro and proposed fix. ETA for patch: earlier this week? (slip) — aiming for next patch Monday.

billing-bot: Automated note: manual credit applied by support (trx_78c4). Amount: 1 free-month.

sam.k: I'll follow up with the customer and close the thread. Thanks all for the quick triage.

tanya: Great teamwork. Add postmortem if we see more occurrences. :thumbsup:
